title: Every Song That Topped the U.K. Chart for 8 or More Weeks, But Didn’t Make the Top 10 on the Hot 100
summary: "Rein Me In” by Sam Fender and Olivia Dean is the first single to log 20 weeks at No. 1 in the U.K. It hasn't even made the top 40 on the Hot 100.
body: UPDATE (Aug. 7): “Rein Me In” by Sam Fender and Olivia Dean logs its 20th nonconsecutive week at No. 1 on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart on the tally that was published on Friday (Aug. 7). The song hasn’t been nearly as big a hit in the U.S. It inches up from No. 69 to No. 68 in its 19th week on the Billboard Hot 100 dated Aug. 8, after climbing as high as No. 64 in April. “Rein Me In” is the first single to log 20 weeks at No. 1 in the U.K., but it has yet to reach the top 10 (or even the top 40) on the Hot 100. In the 68 years that the Hot 100 has been in place, music fans in the U.S. and the U.K. have never been so far apart in their reactions to a song. Here’s an essay on how “Rein Me In” became the U.K.’s longest-running No. 1 single ever. title: Olivia Rodrigo Rocks Out at Surprise Underplay in Brooklyn’s Warsaw: 5 Best Moments
summary: O Rod and her band tore it up one month ahead of The Unraveled Tour's kickoff.
body: When news broke Thursday (Aug. 6) morning that Olivia Rodrigo was playing Brooklyn’s Warsaw — a ballroom-style punk venue nestled in Greenpoint with a capacity of about 1,100 — that very evening, it took less than 30 minutes for the line to start winding around the block as fans biked, Uber-ed and quite literally ran to get in line for tickets, which had to be purchased IRL at the box office. While the venue has played host to plenty of musical legends (Jack White, L7, Stiff Little Fingers, the Prophets of Rage supergroup) over the years, it’s not often a pop star in the midst of their imperial phase performs a one-off underplay like this. (Sam Smith did play Warsaw last winter, but fans had 24 nights to catch them during their residency.) The hourlong wait for tickets in the brutal 80-some-degree heat was beyond worth it. Ahead of her Unraveled Tour kickoff in Hartford, Conn., on Sept. 25, Rodrigo and her band ripped through 15 songs in 62 sweaty, breathtaking minutes, delivering three of her four Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s (“Good 4 U,” “Drop Dead” and “drivers license”) and nine of the 13 songs from You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, her latest (and perhaps bes…

title: Max Styler Was Ready to Quit Dance Music, Now He’s One of Its Buzziest New Artists
summary: The producer's latest EP, I Don't Think I Can Stop, is out today, Aug. 7.
body: Max Styler had been plugging away in dance music for years, and was considering packing it up. “I was sick of my project and thought like, ‘Maybe I’ll just be a ghost producer in the back end, and that’ll be it, because I can’t really figure out what I want to do,” Styler says. Luckily, before that could happen, the California-born artist had a clarifying conversation with the woman who was then his girlfriend and is now his wife. She told him, he recalls, that “‘You just need to make the music you like to listen to and the music people want to dance to.’ She basically told me I needed to make better music.” The simple advice cracked something open for Styler, who, after taking it, has become one of the buzziest new names in dance music. Since 2022, he’s signed tracks to labels including Spinnin Records, John Summit’s Experts Only and Solomun’s Diynamic. He played his first Lollapalooza last weekend, made his Coachella debut in 2025 and is making fans around the world with the extended sets that are his speciality. (“Four hours or more is perfect,” he says of the ideal length.) Today (Aug. 7)…

title: Shueisha Launches 100th-Anniversary MANGA MILLION Project With 400 Titles, Including ‘ONE PIECE’ Free in Over 100 Languages
summary: The service will offer more than 100 languages, including Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, and Korean.
body: Shueisha launched its MANGA MILLION project on Aug. 6, a global digital service commemorating the company’s 100th anniversary. The platform features roughly 400 manga titles translated into more than 100 languages, offering a combined one million pages free of charge to readers worldwide for a limited time. Availability within Japan will be limited to select content. The service requires no registration and is slated to run through the end of December 2027. The lineup includes shonen and seinen titles such as ONE PIECE — translated into 107 languages — along with NARUTO , BLEACH , Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba , Jujutsu Kaisen , Kingdom , OSHI NO KO , SPYxFAMILY , and Chainsaw Man , as well as more than 150 shojo and josei titles including NANA and Kimi ni Todoke : From Me to You . All translations are handled by professional translators, with roughly 300 titles receiving their first-ever English translations. The service will offer over 100 languages, including Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, and Korean. title: Google Messages makes one-handed use much easier with new rollout
summary: The new, redesigned floating context menu and selective text copying make messaging on large phones less frustrating.
body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Google Messages is expanding its server-side rollout of the floating context menu and selective text copying to more beta users. The redesigned floating menu places actions like Reply, Copy, Edit, Star, and Delete in a clean vertical list right by the text bubble for easier one-handed use. Selective text copying introduces draggable handles, allowing users to highlight specific details without copying an entire message. Google Messages finally appears to be expanding a major usability refresh to more users, bringing its redesigned floating context menu and selective text copying to (slightly) wider availability. Reddit user seeareeff reports that they could finally see the new floating context menu when long-pressing a message bubble. Rather than dumping action icons into the top action bar (which forced awkward hand re-gripping on larger phones), the vertical floating menu appears right below/above the text. Essential actions like Reply, Copy, Edit, Star, and Delete are neatly grouped in a clean list format that makes one-handed interaction far less frustrating.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the wrong Samsung foldable to buy this year
summary: It's giving middle-child energy.
body: Samsung gave us two very different foldables this year: the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra . Both these foldables are aimed at completely different people. The Fold 8 introduces a new direction for Samsung with a wider display, a thinner chassis, and a much more compact feel in the hand. Meanwhile, the Fold 8 Ultra carries forward what the Galaxy Z Fold 7 started, refining that familiar formula. Here’s the thing, though: you’d expect two completely different form factors to come with equally different feature sets. Instead, they’re remarkably similar, and the Fold 8 Ultra is priced just $200 more than the Fold 8. That’s exactly what got me thinking. For such a relatively small price increase, the Ultra offers enough extra value that it almost feels like Samsung is nudging buyers in that direction.

body: TL;DR OnePlus has opened the first global ColorOS closed beta for the OnePlus 15 and 15R. The testing program is currently limited to Indian variants and excludes US, EU, and global models. OnePlus hasn’t confirmed the wider rollout yet. OnePlus has officially begun its transition from OxygenOS to ColorOS , opening the first global Closed Beta Testing (CBT) program for the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R. If you’ve been wondering when the software migration announced alongside the company’s withdrawal from the US and European smartphone markets would actually begin, this is the clearest sign yet that it’s now underway. There’s one important catch, though. While both the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R are available in the US, the inaugural ColorOS beta is currently reserved exclusively for Indian variants of the two phones. There’s no mention of the base OS, but Android 17 is expected, given that OnePlus has been testing the OS on the OnePlus 15 since March .

title: Samsung’s latest 200MP sensor could be a fantastic upgrade for Galaxy S27 Ultra

body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has announced the ISOCELL HPC 200MP camera sensor for smartphones. This sensor brings a new pixel structure that enables dramatically improved dynamic range, reduced noise, and more. This would be a significant improvement over the 200MP sensor currently used on Samsung’s Ultra phones. Samsung debuted the first 200MP smartphone camera sensor back in 2022, and it has offered a variety of 200MP sensors since then. The pixels on these sensors are tiny, though, which isn’t great for image quality. However, the company’s latest 200MP camera sensor brings an interesting solution. Samsung has quietly announced the ISOCELL HPC camera sensor (thanks, Dylan H!). At first glance, this 200MP sensor has a lot in common with the ISOCELL HP2 used on the Galaxy S26 Ultra and its predecessors. That means a 1/1.3-inch sensor, 0.6-micron pixels, and Super Quad Phase-Detection autofocus.

title: GrapheneOS isn’t pulling any punches in its beef with Revolut
summary: The gloves are off as GrapheneOS calls Revolut's approach to security "incredibly negligent."
body: Credit: Calvin Wankhede / Android Authority TL;DR GrapheneOS says some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app. The project claims Revolut is specifically targeting GrapheneOS while still supporting outdated Android versions. GrapheneOS suggests a possible workaround but warns that it may not continue to work in the long term. Banking apps can be suspicious of anything that strays from the standard Android experience, but GrapheneOS clearly believes Revolut is taking that distrust way too far. The privacy-focused Android project claims some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app, accusing the fintech company of deliberately trying to shut them out. In a thread on X , GrapheneOS said Revolut is blaming the restriction on security concerns, but argued that the real issue is that they’re enforcing licensing on Google Play . It also questioned how strict Revolut’s security standards can really be when the app still supports Android 9, which launched back in 2018. It went further, describing Revolut as “incredibly negligent when it comes to security.”

title: Maybe the FCC was onto something: These routers are phoning home to China with a secret backdoor
summary: Of course, because they predate the ban, the FCC continues to permit their sale.
body: TL;DR A new report details a massive security flaw in Zbtlink-made routers. The routers are programmed to ping a hard-coded list of servers, traced back to China. Once connected, the routers grant full root access — no authentication required. This past spring, the FCC announced a sweeping ban on new foreign-made routers — like the kind you use to get online with your ISP and connect all your devices to Wi-Fi. This was all done in the name of national security, but just how real of a threat do routers pose? The discovery of a new security vulnerability in some Chinese-made routers may have you looking at the FCC’s action in a slightly more sympathetic light. Jacob Baines at VulnCheck shares his analysis of routers made by Zbtlink, sold under both that and Wiflyer branding. While neither are huge names in the router space, they’re still sold through US retailers like Amazon , and have been around for years — so, plenty of time for these devices to make some inroads on the market.
